specularVerdict: YES, visible for the first time — but only on glass, and it clips. Noon, navy sedan backlight (x855-885,y515) Y 0.774-0.827 against the same pane's body at Y 0.029-0.059: a 14-28x specular peak, plainly a sun glint. Purple SUV backlight (x864-888,y347) Y 0.731-0.853 vs 0.100-0.145. That is a real, measured, SEEN specular response. It is also over-driven: envBoost 1.85 x uEnvComp 1.92 = 3.55x radiance, so the glint saturates to near-white across roughly a quarter of a 45px pane and reads as a bloom blob rather than a windscreen. The PAINT clearcoat, which was the whole assignment, does NOT show a lobe: 17:33 blue sedan roof Y mean 0.1117 / p99 0.1862 (ratio 1.67), magenta roof mean 0.0762 / p99 0.1055 (ratio 1.38 — flat). A ccRoughness 0.05 coat should push p99/mean well past 3 somewhere on a curved panel. clearcoat 1.0 is set and measured, and it produces a broad achromatic sheen, not the 'sharp specular streaks' the reference judge described. Off-sun the panes collapse to a black card: magenta sedan backlight RGB(20,23,34) Y 0.0093 vs MATERIAL_TARGET's 0.04-0.12 floor for a vertical pane. Body-coloured-glass bug IS fixed: blue sedan glass RGB(67,64,79) sat 0.235 vs its paint RGB(52,90,164) sat 0.681.
reference: reference/cs2_05.jpg (street-level parking lot, detailed cars) — the matching frame.

issues.description: Glass sun glint clips. Noon navy sedan backlight peaks Y 0.774-0.827 over ~25x20 px of a ~45 px pane; it reads as a bloom blob, not a reflection. Cause: materials.js RESPONSE_FRAG sets envBoost=1.85 for vCls 2-3 on top of uEnvComp=1/0.519=1.92 (Renderer.js:241), a 3.55x radiance multiplier into a mirror-sharp roughness 0.06 lobe.
issues.fix: Drop glass envBoost 1.85 -> 1.05 and clamp the glass specular: radiance = min(radiance*uEnvComp*envBoost, vec3(0.9)) for vCls 2-3. Raise glass roughness 0.06 -> 0.085 so the sun lobe spreads instead of clipping. Target: pane peak Y 0.25-0.45, never >0.6.

issues.description: Off-sun panes are opaque black cards, the failure MATERIAL_TARGET explicitly forbids. Measured 17:33 detail, magenta sedan backlight RGB(20,23,34) Y 0.0093 — 8x below the 0.04-0.12 vertical-pane floor and 8x darker than the paint above it (Y 0.076). SURFACE_FRAG hard-sets the glass diffuse to vec3(0.0105,0.0125,0.0155), so a pane with no sky in its reflection vector renders black.
issues.fix: Add a Fresnel-independent sky floor in RESPONSE_FRAG for vCls 2-3: sample the environment's upper hemisphere and mix at least 8% of it into the pane regardless of view angle, so every windscreen lands Y 0.04-0.12 in shade with a top-to-bottom gradient.

issues.description: clearcoat 1.0 / ccRoughness 0.05 is set and confirmed by matstats, but produces no visible lobe — only a broad achromatic sheen that also washes the palette pastel. p99/mean on lit paint panels is 1.38-1.67 (blue sedan roof 0.1117/0.1862, magenta roof 0.0762/0.1055). The reference's 'sharp specular streaks' are absent, and the sheen is why saturated palette entries like 0x8e1015 render as salmon.
issues.fix: The lobe is missing because clearcoatRadiance is only multiplied by uEnvComp (materials.js:158) with no boost while the base radiance gets envBoost — the coat sees a half-strength probe. Give the coat its own boost (clearcoatRadiance *= uEnvComp * 1.6) AND add a narrow analytic sun term so a panel whose normal bisects view/sun reaches p99/mean > 3. Then cut the achromatic sheen so dark palette entries stay dark.

issues.description: Wheels are excluded from the shadow map (Renderer.js:221 this.wheels[0].castShadow = false), so there is no darkening under or between the tyres — the reference judge's exact phrase was 'correct contact darkening under the wheels'. What grounds a car is a soft elliptical decal; the cast shadow itself is mostly self-occluded from the showcase camera and its edge spans ~40 px where CS2's is 3-5 px. Measured 15:03: shadow beside the foreground sedan Y 0.018-0.046 vs lit lane Y 0.45-0.52 (good contrast, wrong shape).
issues.fix: Re-enable this.wheels[0].castShadow for LOD 0 only (120 instances, ~4k tris across cascades — affordable inside the 6.1M/8M budget). Tighten the contact decal core (materials.js:369 rounded-rect) to a per-axle pair of ellipses instead of one body-wide blob so the tyre patches read.

issues.description: Chrome/trim at 0.15/1.0 never reads as metal. 17:33 blue sedan rear bumper RGB(56,33,63) Y 0.0337 — DARKER than the paint beside it (Y 0.067); at noon the same part is a flat grey slab Y 0.10-0.28 with no reflection. A metalness-1.0 surface with no diffuse renders black wherever the probe is dim, and envBoost 1.35 is not enough to recover it.
issues.fix: Chrome needs the sky, not a multiplier: give vCls 4 envBoost 2.0 plus a small non-metal floor (metalnessFactor 0.9, a 0.06 grey diffuse) so a bumper still reads as bright trim in shade. Verify: bumper Y should sit ABOVE the adjacent paint at every hour.

issues.description: Against reference/cs2_05.jpg the limiting factor is no longer material response, it is silhouette. CS2 cars have wheel arches, sidewalled tyres, mirrors, door shut-lines, sculpted bumpers and shaped lamps. Ours is a rounded box with a rounded box on top: no arches, wheels barely visible from behind, a full-width grey slab bumper and flat rectangular lamps. At street level this is what a judge sees first.
issues.fix: Add wheel-arch cut-ins and a darkened arch interior to the LOD 0 body loft (VehicleModels.js), split the bumper into a body-colour upper and a dark lower valance, and inset the lamp lenses ~3 cm so they catch a rim highlight. Budget is available: 6.14M of 8M triangles.

issues.description: traffic contributes only 2 rows to matstats and 0 to the <0.2 bucket, because glass/chrome/tyre/lens are shader classes rather than materials. MATERIAL_TARGET mandates verification by matstats, and this module is structurally unverifiable by it.
issues.fix: Register four zero-instance sentinel MeshPhysicalMaterials (traffic/vehicle_glass 0.06, traffic/vehicle_chrome 0.15/1.0, traffic/vehicle_tyre 0.90, traffic/vehicle_lens 0.10) mirroring the shader constants, or teach matstats.mjs to read a material.userData.classes table.

issues.description: scene.environmentIntensity is still 0.5187, unchanged from the pass-4 diagnosis. traffic works around it with uEnvComp = 1/envI, which is precisely why glass over-drives (3.55x) — a workaround stacked on a workaround.
issues.fix: Not traffic's to change alone, but flag it: once environment raises the probe toward 1.0, uEnvComp collapses to 1.0 and the glass boost must be re-tuned or every windscreen will halve. Bake the intended final value now rather than tracking a moving probe.
